text: Rapid landslide mapping with synthetic aperture radar (SAR) must contend with view-dependent backscatter and side-looking geometric distortion. Paired ascending and descending observations can be used during training, although only one orbit may be available for rapid inference. We propose a counter-guided Teacher that uses the complementary orbit to guide a search policy while retrieving evidence only from the target orbit. A target-only Student distills that policy and the retrieved target evidence. We train on all labelled pixels and evaluate the same predictions both with and without excluding geometrically distorted target pixels. On the target-valid region of the Haiti paired-orbit benchmark, the Student improves the area under the precision--recall curve (AUPRC) from 87.55\% to 88.77\% and intersection over union (IoU) from 62.27\% to 64.65\% over its target-only baseline. On the full region, AUPRC rises from 87.98\% to 89.16\% and IoU from 62.91\% to 65.10\%. A separate target-distorted diagnostic shows an IoU gain from 64.14\% to 65.64\%. These results show improved single-orbit mapping across valid and distorted evaluation regions. Complementary guidance is beneficial, although fixed-center sampling remains competitive.

text: We use 1,713 paired Sentinel-1 locations from the Haiti landslide-change dataset \cite{Bralet2024DataPort,Bralet2024}. Each $128\times128$ input stacks pre- and post-event co-polarized (VV) and cross-polarized (VH) backscatter with a constant orbit-indicator channel. The Student uses ConvNeXt-Tiny with an FPN, trained with Adam, learning rate $5\times10^{-5}$, and batch size 16. All labelled pixels contribute to training. At evaluation, we report geometrically valid input-orbit pixels and all pixels from the same predictions. Additional regional analysis considers pixels valid in both views and pixels distorted only in the input view. The area under the precision--recall curve (AUPRC) measures ranking quality; intersection over union (IoU) and F1 use a probability threshold of 0.5.

text: Ours improves the baseline and other current distillation methods in both valid-pixel and full-image evaluation. On pixels valid in both views, its AUPRC/IoU/F1 are 88.15/63.72/77.84\%, compared with 86.91/61.34/76.04\% for the baseline. Distortion therefore affects the evidence available to the model, but does not imply that every such pixel is unclassifiable.

text: Earthquake-triggered landslides can affect inaccessible terrain before field surveys or cloud-free optical images become available. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) supports rapid response through cloud cover and independent of daylight \cite{Mondini2021,Handwerger2022,Amatya2023}. Convolutional and attention-based networks have advanced SAR landslide mapping \cite{Nava2022DL,Nava2022Attention,Boehm2022,Chen2024MFEWF}. Nevertheless, foreshortening, layover, and shadow alter the terrain evidence visible from each radar look direction \cite{Shi2024}; backscatter and speckle also complicate local landslide signatures \cite{Santangelo2022}. Ascending and descending observations therefore provide complementary, rather than interchangeable, views. Requiring both post-event passes can delay the first response map. We instead use paired orbits during training and only the available target orbit during deployment (Fig.~\ref{fig:scenario}).

text: Learning with privileged information \cite{LopezPaz2016} and knowledge distillation (KD) \cite{Hinton2015} provide a basis for transferring training-only observations. Remote-sensing approaches transfer grouped features \cite{Li2022}, multimodal online knowledge \cite{Liu2024}, or frequency and cross-modal affinity information \cite{Sun2027}. Other methods preserve modality-specific information through contrastive distillation \cite{Sikdar2025} or compensate missing features using disentanglement and classwise attention \cite{Kieu2026DIS2}. These approaches motivate a different question for view-dependent SAR: how can an unavailable complementary observation teach a model to exploit evidence that remains observable in the target view?

text: Deformable convolution and attention separate sampling locations and aggregation weights from the sampled values \cite{Dai2017,Zhu2021}. Adaptive aggregation has been applied to remote-sensing segmentation and road extraction \cite{Zuo2022,Dai2023}, while deformable cross-attention addresses weak alignment across imaging modalities \cite{Hu2025}. We use complementary context to guide a target-side search policy; the searched values always come from the target orbit. This prevents a dual-orbit value-fusion path that the deployed Student could not reproduce.
